answeredFailures: Failure 1: the corrected `du` bullet ended '`du -x` and `df -x` are the ones to avoid here', putting `df -x` beside `du -x` as a one-filesystem walk. GNU df has no such flag. Fixed at 04589b7aa2ec80e06846eeeac347476d6df3c44a: `du -x` stays named as the blind walk, which is measured, and the `df -x` half is replaced by the real caveat — df answers for the filesystem that holds the path it is given, so a path under a volume measures that volume and says nothing about the 1 GiB container-filesystem budget, while a path the container filesystem itself holds names `/`, the budgeted one.

Failure 2: the bullet closed 'Verified twice, in two different role containers of this pod, and it is how the 4.4 GiB of Go caches quoted above was found.' The attribution is not in the record. Fixed: the clause is deleted and nothing replaces it; 'Verified twice, in two different role containers of this pod.' stands, and the 4.4 GiB figure keeps its place in the Evidence paragraph above, which is what the record does support.
The same `df -x` clause was in the pull request body's `E2E (implementer)` line, which squashes into main's commit message, and is corrected there too.

No permanent test, for the reasons the tester, the architect and this role have already recorded: a grep over prose is a source-text test this repository's conventions forbid, and the repository has no checker over docs/solutions/.

proof.criterion: Failure 1: the note no longer names a df flag that does not exist, and the caveat that replaces it is the measured one.
proof.surface: A live Legion role container — this issue's own implementer container in its Agent Sandbox pod, the same surface the note is about.
proof.observed: `df -x` prints `df: option requires an argument -- 'x'` and `Try 'df --help' for more information.` — GNU df's -x is --exclude-type and takes an argument, so there is no one-filesystem df. `df -x /` is read as 'exclude filesystems of type /', excludes nothing and prints 21 lines, the header and every mount of the container. `df -k --output=target,used` names `/legion` for /legion (652476 KiB) and `/` for both /home/legion/.cache and / (38176 KiB each, the same figure), which is exactly the caveat the note now states: df answers for the filesystem holding the path, so a path under a volume measures that volume while a path the container filesystem holds measures the budget.
proof.negativeControl: The architect's own example for this clause was that `df ~/.cache` says nothing about the budget. Measured, it does: /home/legion/.cache and / report the same mount point and the same used figure, because ~/.cache is on the container filesystem. The note therefore states the volume case (/legion) and not that example — the measurement refused half the instruction, which is the whole point of the clause it replaces, and the architect was told.
proof.deviationFromInstruction: The architect asked for 'df /legion or df ~/.cache says nothing about the 1 GiB budget'. Only the /legion half is true here, so the note carries that half alone.
